# 1.28.0 — one safety gate for every tool, plans and schedules, remote machines, spending limits and Windows integration

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are.

## Settings

Settings are compact again: 690×520 and ten pages, laid out as in 1.27. Remote computers and MCP
servers are tabs of **Automation**. Bigger blocks — spending limits, backups, storage and cleanup,
the list of tools, Windows integration and voice input — open as their own pages from a row with
›, so every page reads top to bottom without a wall of text. Esc goes back.

Every pop-up window now shares one look: the title says what is being asked, fields have labels,
and an error or "Checking…" appears next to the buttons, so the window no longer jumps.
Destructive buttons are red, and no system message boxes are left. Tabs, folders and the PC health
panel no longer shift when you switch, expand or refresh them.

## One gate for every tool

Until now the chat's own tools went around the protection the agent had: writing a file from the
chat asked nothing and was not checked by SynGuard. Now every tool call — from the chat and from
the agent — passes one gate: the access mode, switched-off tools, hard refusals, SynGuard, your
confirmation, a snapshot for rollback and a line in the audit log.

- **Writing files.** Only a new file in Downloads or on the Desktop is written without a
  question. Overwriting a file, or writing anywhere else, asks first. Anything inside the
  program's own data folder (settings, keys, chats, instructions, the audit log) is refused to
  every tool.
- **Access modes** — the new **Settings → Security** page: *Normal*, *Ask about everything*,
  *Read only* and *Approve everything automatically*. The same page switches individual chat and
  agent tools off; a switched-off tool is not even shown to the model.
- **Allow for a while.** The confirmation window can allow a tool until the end of the reply or
  for the whole chat. PowerShell can only be allowed until the end of the reply.
- **PowerShell is read, not guessed.** A script is now analysed by its syntax tree, and only
  reading runs without a question. The confirmation window lists what the script is going to
  change. Downloads from sites outside the allowlist and account changes that cannot be checked
  are refused with a hint to use the dedicated tool.
- **Hands off the essentials.** Critical Windows processes and services (lsass, csrss, winlogon,
  Windows Defender, the firewall, RPC and more) and the program itself cannot be stopped.
  Browser password and cookie stores, SSH and GPG keys, password vaults, Windows credential
  stores and the SAM/SECURITY hives are not read by any tool.
- **SynGuard failures are visible.** If the safety check could not run or its answer could not be
  read, the tool round says so instead of looking checked.

## Audit log

Every call that changes the system and every refusal is written to an audit log in the profile
folder: time, chat, agent, tool, arguments (secrets removed), outcome, who allowed it and what
SynGuard said. Reading is not logged. The log lives on when chats are deleted, has its own
**Audit** tab in the journal with CSV and JSON export, and travels in the data archive.

## Rollback that really rolls back

- A snapshot now records the registry keys the change touches, value by value. Rolling back
  returns changed values **and removes values and keys added after the snapshot**.
- Services and scheduled tasks are compared with the snapshot and only what differs is touched;
  tasks created during the reply are removed. Startup entries (Run keys) come back too.
- The **Snapshots** tab shows what a rollback will return before you confirm it, lists Windows
  restore points and opens System Restore.
- Re-enabling or disabling a scheduled task during rollback used a wrong command and did nothing;
  fixed.

## Answer versions

**Retry** and editing your question no longer throw away what came after. The previous answer —
with everything that followed it — stays as a version: switch between them with the ‹ 2/3 ›
arrows under the message. Only the version on screen is sent to the model; spending, the journal
and the images of all versions are kept. A version can be deleted on its own.

## Privacy

- **Encrypt conversations on disk** (Settings → Security): chats, the chat list and new audit log
  entries are stored encrypted with Windows' own means (DPAPI) and can only be read under your
  Windows account. Existing chats are rewritten in the background, and both formats always read.
- **Auto-lock** after 5–60 minutes without input, and **Lock now** — for a profile with a
  password. Replies and agent work carry on under the lock screen; the completion notification
  no longer shows the reply's text while locked.
- **Password on the data archive.** Export can protect the `.amrnbak` file with a password
  (AES-256-GCM). A damaged, cut or reshuffled archive is detected, and a wrong password is told
  apart from damage.
- **Delete all data** now works. It asks twice (the second time you type a word), then the
  program restarts and removes the profile's chats, settings, keys, instructions and appearance.
  Other profiles and interface translations stay. The audit log is removed only if you tick the
  box for it.

## The agent: plans, schedules, recipes, other machines

- **Plan first.** For the tiers you choose (by default only heavy tasks) the agent first looks
  around with read-only tools and sends a plan: steps with the tool, action and target. You
  **Run**, **Cancel** or **Amend** it with a remark. An approved step runs without another
  question only if the call matches it exactly; anything off the plan asks as usual, and
  SynGuard always asks. Settings → Security.
- **"What will change".** The confirmation window now shows a dry run with `-WhatIf` — only when
  every changing command in the script supports it. External programs and .NET calls get no dry
  run, because `-WhatIf` would not stop them.
- **Stop means stop.** Stopping a reply now ends running PowerShell scripts and external programs
  at once, instead of waiting for their time-out.
- **New actions**, all confirmed and, where possible, with a snapshot for rollback: service start
  type (including delayed start); turning startup entries off and on the way Task Manager does;
  installing, hiding and pausing Windows updates (no automatic restart); DNS servers and the
  `hosts` file; network adapters, Wi-Fi profiles, `traceroute`, Winsock and IP reset; turning
  devices on and off and rolling a driver back; a Defender quick scan and signature update;
  Remote Desktop on and off; searching files by mask, size and date; writing to the clipboard
  (never BitLocker keys, passwords or API keys). Disks, keyboards, mice and system devices are
  never turned off.
- **Instructions for the agent.** An instruction can now be shown to the agent too (the
  **Agent** switch in its editor). Closed ones stay invisible to it.
- **Recipes** (Settings → Automation): save an action from the journal and run it later without
  a model — through the same confirmation, snapshot and audit log. Parameters are written as
  `{{name}}`. **Via the agent** starts a new chat with the task instead.
- **Scheduled tasks** (Settings → Automation → Schedule): daily, on chosen weekdays, every N hours
  or at startup. A run is **read-only**: the agent checks and reports, and anything it would
  change goes into the report as advice. Each run leaves a chat and, when it found something, a
  notification. A ready-made "PC health check" is included.
- **PC health** panel: a short summary like System Information. One line on top says how the
  computer is doing and which areas need a look; below it the disks (with free-space bars, as in
  Explorer, and drive health), processor, memory and uptime, Defender and the firewall, errors of
  the last day and pending updates. Only values that need attention are coloured. An area with
  something to look at has **Look into it**, which starts a chat with a request the model can act
  on by itself: what was checked on this PC, what was found and what to do.
- **Run as administrator** by clicking the warning icon. The chat and your unsent text come
  back after the restart.
- **Remote computers** (Settings → Automation → Computers): a chat can target another computer over
  PowerShell Remoting — WinRM with a login and password, or SSH with a key (needs PowerShell 7).
  Only PowerShell runs remotely; other tools refuse with a hint instead of running on this PC.
  The password goes to PowerShell through its input, never on a command line. The confirmation
  window names the machine.
- **MCP servers** (Settings → Automation → MCP): tools of Model Context Protocol servers — local
  (stdio) or over HTTP — become agent tools. Every call asks until you mark that tool read-only;
  server answers are treated as data, not instructions. Secrets are stored encrypted and are not
  included in data archives.

## Chats

- **Find in a chat** with Ctrl+F: a counter, arrows, highlighting, and the matching message opens
  and scrolls into view — tool blocks included.
- **Search the text of all chats** for free: a new **Text** mode in the side panel, backed by an
  index on this PC (encrypted when chats are). A click opens the chat at the message.
- **Organise chats:** folders, coloured tags, an archive, sorting by change, creation, name or
  cost, and selecting several chats with Ctrl/Shift for moving, tagging, archiving or deleting.
  Folders have their own heading, and an open folder is one card with its chats inside. You pick
  a tag's colour, and the ⋯ next to a tag in any menu renames, recolours or deletes it. Sorting
  and the tag filter live in the ⇅ menu next to the search; an active filter shows as one pill
  that clears it. The side panel's width can be dragged and is remembered.
- **Export** a chat to Markdown, a self-contained HTML page, PDF or the printer — the branch on
  screen, optionally with tool calls and prices, up to a chosen message.
- **Work report:** the request, every action word for word with its result and who allowed it,
  and the rollback snapshots are gathered by the program; the model only adds "what was wrong"
  and "what was checked" from those facts.
- **Commands** at the start of the input field: `/new`, `/model`, `/compact`, `/export`,
  `/instr`, `/recipe`, `/readonly`, `/agent`. `/readonly` keeps the chat and its agents from
  changing anything.
- **Compact the context:** the older part of a long chat goes to the model as a summary, the last
  two exchanges verbatim; the messages stay on screen. Offered from the context ring and when a
  provider says the context is too long.
- **Per-chat settings:** a chat can have its own prompt and set of instructions (the chat's ⋯
  menu → Chat settings).
- **A draft per chat:** typed text, quotes and attachments stay with their chat and survive a
  restart — switching chats no longer carries your text into the other one.
- **Code blocks:** save to a file, wrap lines, optional line numbers, and **Run via the agent** for
  PowerShell and batch code (it goes through the usual confirmation).
- **Voice input:** a microphone button (click, or hold to talk; Ctrl+Shift+M). Speech is
  recognised on this PC by Windows' own recognisers when your language has one, or in the cloud
  by a transcription model of Venice or OpenRouter; the button shows only when one of them is
  available. The text goes into the field and is never sent by itself.
- **Drop files anywhere** on the window to attach them.
- Your messages show the time they were sent.
- **Hotkeys:** Ctrl+K search chats, Ctrl+Shift+R retry, Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab next and
  previous chat, Ctrl+Shift+C copy the last answer, Ctrl+B side panel, Ctrl+, settings,
  Ctrl+Shift+H PC health, Ctrl+/ list of all shortcuts. Esc stops the reply when the field is
  empty; ↑ in an empty field brings back your last message.

## Money

- **Spending limits** per day and month, for the whole profile or a single key, and a cap per
  reply (with its agents) and per scheduled run. Inside a reply, reaching a limit asks whether to
  continue; outside one it refuses. A warning comes at 80% (adjustable). Settings → Key & Info →
  Limits and alerts.
  Limits count dollars from the program's own spending log; Diem is not counted.
- **Price estimate** next to the context ring before you send: "≈ $0.03", with the range from
  the cheapest to the dearest model for *Auto*. Agents, web search, images and PDFs are not in
  the estimate, and the tooltip says so.
- **Cost of the whole chat** — "Σ $…" by the input field, with a breakdown by model, agents,
  tools, safety checks, titles and summaries, and in the tooltip of each chat in the list.
- **Balance thresholds** are now settings (overall and per key), and crossing one downwards
  sends a notification.
- **Export spending to CSV** from the chart, in the separator and decimal format of your region.
- **OpenRouter guide** next to the Venice one on the Info page.

## Your data

- **Backup copies of settings, profiles and keys.** A damaged file is set aside and replaced by
  the last good copy instead of being silently overwritten with defaults — you are told when it
  happens.
- **Automatic backups** of all data daily or weekly to a folder of your choice (by default
  Documents\Amarin Admin AI Backups), keeping the last N. Keys are not included. The backups are
  not encrypted even when chats are — the page says so.
- **Keeping chats tidy:** archive or delete chats untouched for N days (at least a week; pinned
  and open chats are never touched), clean up crash logs, old rollback snapshots (the last 5
  stay), exports and cached backgrounds, and see the largest chats.
- **Attachments are stored as separate files** next to the chat instead of inside it, so the
  chat file itself stays small and one image used twice is stored once. Old chats are read as
  they are; **Rewrite** converts them.

## Windows integration

- **Tray icon** with a status dot (answering, waiting for your confirmation, a background error)
  and a menu. The close button can hide the window to the tray instead of quitting.
- **Notifications:** the program's own card, as before, or Windows notifications. New: a
  question about a risky action while the window is out of sight, spending limits, balance and
  backups.
- **Global shortcuts:** show or hide the window (Win+Shift+A by default), a new chat with the
  clipboard text, a new chat with a screenshot. A shortcut Windows already uses is reported.
- **Start with Windows** straight into the tray.
- **"Ask Amarin"** in Explorer's menu for files, folders and folder backgrounds. On Windows 11 it
  is under "Show more options": the new menu accepts only packaged apps.
- **Jump list:** new chat, PC health and the five latest chats.

## Accessibility and language

- Screen readers now get a name for every icon button, switch and picker, and the keyboard focus
  is drawn in the accent colour.
- **Follows Windows high contrast** (on by default), switching without a restart.
- **Chat text size** (four steps) and **code font** (Consolas, Cascadia Mono, Courier New).
- **Edit a machine translation** of the interface: search, fix a line, re-translate one line. Lines
  you fixed are kept, and later re-translations neither send nor pay for them. A line whose
  `{0}` placeholders do not match is not saved.

## Updates

An update is installed only when its SHA-256 checksum is known — from GitHub or from the
`SHA256SUMS` file that now comes with every release — and the file is checked once more right
before it replaces the program, including the step that runs as administrator. A release without
a checksum is never installed by itself; you can still install it with a separate confirmation.
If the program you run is signed, the new version must carry a valid signature of the same
publisher.

- **Release notes before installing:** the update question shows what the new version brings.
- **Beta channel** (Settings → Updates): also offers pre-releases. A beta user is offered the
  final release of the same number.
- **Go back to the previous version:** after a successful update the old program is kept next to
  it, and one button puts it back. Automatic updates will not reinstall the version you left;
  going back to a version older than this one turns automatic updates off, because it would
  reinstall it otherwise.
- **What's new** is shown once after an update.
- **Report a problem** from the crash window or the Info page opens a GitHub issue form with the
  report already filled in — without your profile path, user name or computer name. You read it
  and submit it yourself. **Open the log folder** is next to it.

## Smaller changes

- **Command line:** `--prompt` now only puts the text into the input field, both on first start
  and when the program is already open. To send it right away, add `--send`. Scripts that relied
  on automatic sending need the new flag.
- **Hotkeys:** a new chat is now **Ctrl+N**; Ctrl+F is free. If you had assigned Ctrl+N to
  something else yourself, your assignment wins.
- **No key yet?** Sending, retrying and continuing now show a notice with a button to
  **Key & Info** instead of a system message box — and Retry no longer erases the answer first.
- **Scheduled tasks** are created only with a known schedule; quotes in a task name are refused.
- **Long repairs:** DISM may run for up to an hour and SFC for 30 minutes, and cancelling the reply
  stops them.
- **English interface:** the confirmation window, agent statuses, sharing, the image viewer, the
  crash window and provider errors are no longer in Russian. The agent writes its explanations
  in the interface language.
- The agent's built-in instructions no longer contain a policy about one particular company's
  software, and its list of commands now names `/agent lite|fast|heavy`. An unchanged saved copy
  of the old instructions is replaced by the new ones.
- **Several launches in a row** (a jump list, Explorer, a shortcut) are now handled in the order
  they happened; before, any of them could win.

## File

`Amarin-Admin-AI-v1.28.0-win-x64.exe` — a single file, nothing to unpack, plus `SHA256SUMS` with
its checksum. The file is about 12 MB larger than 1.27: about 10 MB is the PowerShell parser, and
about 2 MB the rest of this release, speech recognition included.
